newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Akzo Nobel fibres hurt by viscose, Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Akzo Nobel fibres hurt by viscose, Brazil.

text.p: Chemical group Akzo Nobel NV said on Wednesday profits at its fibres business had been dragged down by poor results for viscose textiles and a disappointing performance from its Brazilian operations.
Nevertheless the fibres arm had managed to stay in profit in a traditionally weak quarter, finance director Syb Bergsma told a third-quarter results news conference.
Akzo said in August it expected its fibres unit to break even in the third quarter.
Akzo earlier reported third quarter operating profits at its fibres division fell to two million guilders from 15 million in the second quarter and 28 million in the year-earlier quarter.
"Viscose textile yarns suffered from sharp price competition from eastern Europe and the Far East," Bergsma said.
Akzo's yarns were of superior quality, but at the edge of the market it had lost sales because of massive price undercutting, he said.
Sales had also been pressured due to falling demand from the fashion industry, but this was seen as temporary. "We continue to believe in viscose, but we must cut costs," Bergsma said.
He said Akzo would significantly improve margins with the relocation of its Dutch and German viscose textile finishing operations to Gorzow, Poland, announced in January.
The relocation will be undertaken in three phases, the first of which, involving 600 jobs, would be complete in 1997.
"We will begin textile finishing in Gorzow next year," Bergsma said. The operation, involving 1,800 jobs in total, will be completed by the year 2000, he said.
Akzo's Brazilian operations continued to suffer from lower demand arising from the government's abolition of import tariffs, particularly for the car industry.
However barriers for raw materials such as caprolactam had not been taken down, so its COBAFI tyre-fibres unit was being squeezed at both ends, Bergsma said.
Akzo was taking steps to slim down the workforce at the plant, he added.
Also in Brazil, Akzo's Polyenka textile yarns plant had suffered from poor market conditions, but in the meantime demand looked to be picking up, Bergsma said.
